questions.q: Why does this lesson say a 9-to-5 SOC leaves real gaps in coverage?
options: SIEM software stops working outside business hours
Regulations only require monitoring during business hours
Automated attacks run continuously and attackers often favor off-hours, weekends, and holidays precisely because fewer defenders are watching then
Logs are only generated between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m.
questions.explain: Attackers specifically pick times when they expect fewer eyes watching and slower response.

options: A single analyst working literally 24 hours straight without a break
Scheduling shifts based on the amount of daylight in one city
Handing off SOC monitoring between offices in different time zones so one region's end-of-day is another's start
A model used only for physical, not digital, security
questions.explain: Regional SOCs each staff their own normal business hours, relaying the queue as one region's day ends and another's begins.

questions.q: In a rotating shift schedule at a single-location SOC, what rotates?
options: The SOC's physical office location changes every week
Analysts cycle through day, evening, and overnight shifts over time, rather than one person being stuck permanently on nights
Nothing rotates — the same analyst always works the same shift
The organization's security tooling changes shift by shift
questions.explain: Rotating schedules spread the burden of overnight coverage across the whole team instead of one person bearing it indefinitely.

questions.q: What problem does on-call escalation solve?
options: It replaces the need for a SIEM entirely
It is only used for scheduling vacation time
It backstops a smaller after-hours team by making specific Tier 2/3 staff reachable when something exceeds that smaller team's authority
It eliminates the need for any after-hours staff at all
questions.explain: A smaller overnight team can page an on-call analyst with more access or authority when an alert exceeds what they can handle alone.

questions.q: A mid-size company has one office and can't staff a full overnight shift. Which realistic combination fits the models in this lesson?
options: Opening SOCs on three continents immediately
Running zero monitoring overnight and hoping nothing happens
A smaller overnight presence backstopped by on-call escalation to a Tier 2/3 analyst
Requiring every analyst to work 24 hours straight, every day
questions.explain: A reduced after-hours team paired with on-call escalation is the realistic single-office solution this lesson describes.
